extension.description: Close the lid, keep your AI agents running. Turns the screen off and keeps the computer awake until you come back, with battery and temperature guards and e-mail notifications.
view.name: Sleepwalker
command.startUntilReturn: Start sleepwalking until I come back
command.startWhileAgent: Start sleepwalking while the agent works
command.startTimer: Start sleepwalking for a set time…
config.lockScreen: Lock the screen when a session starts.
config.turnOffDisplay: Turn the display off when a session starts.
config.displayOffDelaySeconds: Normally the screen locks/turns off only when you close the lid. This delay is just the fallback used on machines with no lid sensor.
config.returnGraceSeconds: Keyboard and mouse input during the first seconds is ignored, so the click that starts a session does not end it.
config.endAction: What to do with the computer when a session ends on its own (agent finished, time up, battery or temperature limit). When you come back yourself, nothing happens.
config.endAction.hibernate: Hibernate (falls back to sleep when hibernation is off).
config.maxHours: Safety limit: any session ends after this many hours.
config.agent.idleMinutes: *While the agent works* mode: minutes without terminal commands or agent CPU activity before the session ends.
config.agent.watchTerminals: Count running terminal commands (VS Code shell integration) as agent activity.
config.agent.watchProcesses: Process names that count as agents when they use CPU. On Linux, agents started through `node` or `python` are recognized by their script path too.
config.agent.cpuThresholdPercent: CPU use (percent of one core) above which a watched process counts as working.
config.guardrails.minBatteryPercent: End the session and put the computer to sleep below this battery level when not plugged in. `0` turns this off.
config.guardrails.maxTemperatureC: End the session and put the computer to sleep at this temperature (°C). `0` turns this off. On Windows, temperature sensors usually need VS Code to run as administrator.
config.email.enabled: Send e-mail notifications. Set them up from the Sleepwalker panel; the password is kept in VS Code's secret storage.
config.email.from: Sender shown in the e-mail. Defaults to the SMTP user name.
config.email.smtpSecure: Use SSL/TLS from the start (port 465). When off, STARTTLS is required.
config.email.smtpUser: SMTP user name, usually your e-mail address.
